title: Adaptive query-plan profiling and zero-downtime schema change pipeline for control-plane DB
creator: Maya Patel
description: Problem: Our control-plane Postgres cluster still incurs high p99 read latency on several dashboard and enrollment queries during rolling deploys and index rebuilds. We've been performing ad-hoc migrations that cause brief spikes in replica lag and occasional index bloat. Previous tickets focused on index rewriting and compaction, but we lack an automated, low-risk path for multi-step schema changes (rename + backfill + drop) and a live way to measure query-plan regressions before rollout. This ticket proposes building two coordinated pieces: 1) an adaptive query-plan profiling system that captures representative plans across production tenants and flags plan shape changes when a migration or index change is tested, and 2) a zero-downtime schema change pipeline that uses shadow writes, phased backfills, and safe roll-forward/rollback hooks to apply complex changes without impacting SLOs.
acceptance_criteria: Profiling: collect sampled query plans and runtime stats for top 2000 control-plane queries over a 24h window
Detection: automatic alert when a candidate schema change causes >10% median p50/p95 latency regression on profiled queries in staging
Migrations: implement a migration runner that performs shadow writes, background backfills, and online index builds with progress reporting
Safety: include an automated rollback path that can stop a migration and re-route traffic to previous schema variant within 5 minutes
Observability: dashboard with before/after plan diff, tokenized plan fingerprints, and per-tenant regression summaries
Docs: migration runbook and playbook for on-call with rollback steps and post-mortem checklist
implementation_steps: Design query-plan fingerprinting format (plan hash + operator histogram + major cardinalities) and storage TTL
Instrument production read queries to sample EXPLAIN ANALYZE plans at low qps (adaptive sampling based on query frequency)
Build a staging harness to replay sampled queries against candidate schema changes and capture plan diffs
Create a migration runner service that performs: shadow write mode -> background backfill -> migrate reads to new projection -> schedule index builds -> finalize and drop legacy columns
Integrate a progress API and safety gates (max replica lag, max backfill write amplification, time window constraints)
Add UI panel in Console for migration telemetry and plan diffs; surface tenant-level risk and rollback buttons
Run 2 canary migrations (small tables then medium tables) in dedicated window and verify metrics
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: sampling overhead increases CPU on primary. Mitigation: adaptive sampling and offload explain analysis to a separate read-replica pool
Risk: background backfill writes cause increased replication lag. Mitigation: rate-limit backfills and use burst windows during low-traffic hours
Risk: plan regression not visible for low-volume tenants. Mitigation: include synthetic traffic replay for low-volume paths in staging
Risk: migration runner bug causes partial writes. Mitigation: transactional shadow write fencing and idempotency markers; require integration tests
observability_and_metrics: Collected: plan_hash, wall_time_ms, planning_time_ms, rows_estimated_vs_actual, operator_counts
Dashboards: migration progress, replica lag, backfill write throughput, query latency p50/p95/p99 by fingerprint
Alerts: plan-change-regression (>10% p95 increase), replica-lag-threshold, backfill-error-rate
notes: We intentionally keep profiling lightweight: capture plans for a sampled subset of top traffic and aggregate to plan fingerprints rather than storing full text for every call.
Align window with SRE: prefer night maintenance windows for heavy backfill phases; explore tenant-based throttling for customers on Dedicated plans.
This complements previous index compaction work but differs by focusing on migrations that require coordinated read/write changes (column renames, denormalizations, and projection flattening).
